formula: noun, who/which + clause, (non-defining, commas) · noun + who/that + clause (defining, no commas) · noun + -ing / -ed (reduced) · ..., which + comment · preposition + whom/which
formula_visual: [My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting] // [the man standing there]
when_to_use: Non-defining clauses add EXTRA information, take commas, and cannot use 'that'. Defining clauses identify which one and take no commas. Reduced relatives drop 'who is'/'that was' and leave just -ing (active) or -ed (passive). 'which' can also comment on a whole clause.
when_to_use_ar: غير المحدِّدة تضيف معلومة إضافية بفواصل ولا تستخدم that. والمحدِّدة تحدّد أيّهم بدون فواصل. والمختصرة تحذف who is وتترك -ing أو -ed. و'which' يمكنها التعليق على الجملة كلها.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic relative clauses repeat the object pronoun (الرجل الذي رأيته), producing 'the man who I saw him'. Arabic also has no comma-based distinction between essential and extra information, so learners add or omit commas randomly, which changes the meaning in English.

examples.en: My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting us.
examples.ar: أخي، الذي يسكن في دبي، سيزورنا (إضافة)

examples.en: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
The man standing over there is my uncle.
He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.
The person to whom I spoke was helpful.
examples.ar: الشخص الذي تحدثت إليه كان مفيدًا (رسمي)

common_errors.wrong: The man who I saw him was tall.
common_errors.correct: The man who I saw was tall.
common_errors.explanation: Don't repeat the object pronoun after the relative pronoun.

common_errors.wrong: My brother, that lives in Dubai, is visiting.
common_errors.correct: My brother, who lives in Dubai, is visiting.
common_errors.explanation: 'that' cannot be used in non-defining clauses.

common_errors.wrong: He arrived late, that annoyed everyone.
common_errors.correct: He arrived late, which annoyed everyone.
common_errors.explanation: Use 'which' to comment on a whole clause, never 'that'.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: My brother, ___ lives in Dubai, is visiting.
The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
The man ___ (stand) over there is my uncle. (reduced)

quick_rule: Extra info → commas + who/which (never 'that'). Essential info → no commas. Reduced → drop 'who is', keep -ing (active) or -ed (passive). Comment on a clause → 'which'.
quick_rule_ar: معلومة إضافية → فواصل + who/which (لا that). معلومة أساسية → بدون فواصل. المختصرة → احذف who is وأبقِ -ing أو -ed.
mnemonic: Commas = extra, no commas = essential. 'that' only lives in defining clauses.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 11 you drilled the parenthetical pitch drop. Non-defining clauses must be SPOKEN as a parenthesis — pause, drop, pause — or your listener hears a defining clause and a different meaning.
